resources.string: OnPath shows your map offline, plans your route and guides you on the way. For the dot on the map and the guidance it needs a few things from your phone. It takes about a minute – or do it later, when you start a tour.
OnPath can show where you are, record your tour and guide you.
You can set the rest up any time in Settings → Phone setup.
A tour needs your precise location. You can still plan and look at the map.
Your phone removed this because OnPath was not used for some months. That is normal – set it up again here.
This was switched off since you last used OnPath.
So the map shows where you are, and your tour is recorded and guided. Your position stays on your phone.
On the next screen, allow OnPath while you use the app – with precise location.
No problem – the map and planning work without it. For the dot on the map and a tour OnPath needs your location.
Android does not ask again. Tap Continue, then Permissions → Location, and allow it while using the app, with precise location.
For your track and the turn hints OnPath needs your exact position – an approximate one can be off by a kilometre or more.
On the next screen, change to precise location.
Your phone's location is switched off, so no app can find your position.
Tap Continue and switch location on.
While you record, a notification shows that OnPath is working and lets you pause. With the screen off it also asks when you leave the route.
Tap Continue and switch notifications for OnPath on.
With the phone in your pocket OnPath tells you about turns: one buzz = left, two buzzes = right.
Hold the phone in your hand and tap Test.
Did you feel one buzz, then two?

Then your phone's vibration is turned down or off. On Pixel phones: Settings → Sound & vibration → Vibration & haptics → switch on Alarm vibration. On other phones look for vibration under Sound. Then test again.
This phone cannot vibrate. OnPath shows turns on the screen and in the notification.
Your phone restricts OnPath in the background. It may stop recording when the screen is off.
Tap Continue, then Battery (or App battery usage), and choose Unrestricted or Optimized – not Restricted.
Phones from %1$s close apps in the background to save battery. These settings keep OnPath recording – the names can differ a little on your phone.

1. Settings → Battery → Background usage limits: switch off “Put unused apps to sleep”.\n2. OnPath must not be in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps” – add it to “Never sleeping apps”.\n3. App settings → Battery → Unrestricted.
1. App settings → Autostart: on.\n2. App settings → Battery saver → No restrictions.\n3. Open the recent apps, hold OnPath (or pull it down) and tap the lock.
1. Settings → Battery → App launch → OnPath: switch to Manage manually.\n2. Switch on all three: Auto-launch, Secondary launch, Run in background.

1. App settings → Battery → Don't optimize (or Allow background activity).\n2. Open the recent apps and lock OnPath.\n3. If OnPath still stops: Settings → Battery → Battery optimization → ⋮ → switch off Advanced optimization.
On this phone battery saver turns GPS off when the screen goes off. Your track would have gaps.
Turn battery saver off for the tour – or keep the screen on.
When you don't use OnPath for a while
Android removes access from apps you have not opened for some months. OnPath then simply asks again. If you want it to keep working at the start of the season, switch this off.
Tap Continue and switch off the setting for unused apps (on Pixel: “Pause app activity if unused”).
On – after a long break OnPath asks again
What OnPath needs from your phone, and why. Tap a line to set it up or to read more.
